messages:
marta: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel bump we started seeing a 6% drop in prefix cache hit rate for short chat flows. Not sure if it's keying or warmup timing.
liam: Oh yikes. Which cohort? customer-facing chat or internal tests?
sana: Looks like prod chat (cohort=steady_short). I just pulled a perf profile. Kernel changes shifted batch boundaries and we observe earlier eviction of small prefixes.
kai: That could be the batching heuristic changing sequence alignment — small requests now land in batches with different pad lengths, altering the effective probe keys.
marta: Right. I also noticed tool call fields are being serialized differently in a handful of requests (ordering + absent nulls). Might change the canonical key.
liam: Can you paste an example of the old vs new key? Even a pseudocode diff helps.
sana: Old canonicalization: ````
normalize(prompt): strip_ws(lowercase), sort_object_keys(tool_args), trim_trailing_newline
key = sha256(model + tokenizer_version + normalize(prompt) + system_prompt_hash)
````

sana: New-ish behavior after kernel bump: we don't apply sort_object_keys for tool args when the request goes through the fast-path encoder; ordering preserved. So same prompt body but different key.
kai: Ah — partial canonicalization depends on code path. That's bad. We should not have key generation depend on encoder path.
marta: Agreed. Proposal: move full canonicalizer upstream — early in request handling — so keying always sees the same normalized payload. Also pin tokenizer_version when generating keys (explicit field in cache key).
liam: Tokenizer pin makes sense. We already include model name but tokenizer drift has been subtle. Add a tokenizer checksum if possible.
sana: Quick experiment: I re-generated keys for 10k samples with forced upstream normalization + tokenizer_pin and hit rate recovered +4.8% in that cohort.
marta: Nice. Does that require API changes for private deployments? We can't break existing keys for customers who relied on old path.
kai: We can make it a rollout: default to backward-compatible keying with a new toggle flag in request meta like `key_version=2`. For hosted, flip on canary servers first. For Dedicated/Private, it's opt-in.
liam: Also need to audit system prompt inclusion. We have a recent change where system_prompt is normalized (trim) in some code paths and not in others. That could cause key splits even if user prompt identical.
sana: I found ~1200 keys where only difference was system_prompt whitespace. Heatmap attached in my gist: https://gist.github.com/xxxx (link).
marta: Can we add tolerant matching fallback? If key miss, check a relaxed-normalizer probe before declaring cold start? Might be expensive.
kai: We already have a short-lived probe cache tier — but probing adds latency. Maybe do it only for low-latency-sensitive routes or when cold-starts exceed threshold.
liam: For tooling: let's add a lightweight canonicalizer (strip bs, deterministic tool arg ordering, include tokenizer_pin) in the request ingress. Keep old key generator available under `key_version=1`.
sana: I'll prepare a micro benchmark: compare hit rate and p50/p95 latency for key_v1 vs key_v2 on the steady_short and longform cohorts.
marta: Can we also add telemetry tagging for cases where tool args ordering differs? I want metrics to drive backfill and warmup decisions.
kai: Add a small histogram: `cache_key_variants_per_req` and a counter `probe_after_miss_recovered`.
liam: Deploy plan: canary on 10% of hosts with key_v2 ingress + warmup backfill for likely-hot prefixes. If stable, ramp to 50% then 100%. For Dedicated/Private, ship docs + opt-in param.
marta: One more note — tooling for reproducing key mismatches: I wrote a tiny script that replays requests through both canonicalizers and emits diffed keys. I'll drop it in the repo.
sana: Great. I'll run replay overnight and post results in morning.
deploy-bot: deploy finished on canary cluster (canary-42) — image: runtime:v2026.03.18-canary-keyv2 — health OK. :rocket:
liam: Thanks — let's sync tomorrow after the replay. If numbers look good we can start the warmup backfill job. :thumbsup:
